BLISSAIR, based in Bocholt, Germany, is an aviation company, providing customized air transport solutions and aviation services.

BLISSAIR stands for safe, fast, and comfortable private air travel worldwide, delivered through our own aircraft fleet as well as an extensive network of partner aircraft.

Our facilities in Bocholt have recently been expanded to include a CAE Full-Flight Simulator for the King Air B200 equipped with a Pro Line 21 cockpit. A second simulator is already in the planning stage.

The simulator provides a highly realistic representation of the aircraft and is certified to the highest qualification standard, Level D. This gives BLISSAIR a unique market position, as it is the only simulator of its kind in Europe.

To support the ongoing maintenance and operation of this simulator, we are looking for an enthusiastic aviation-minded team player to join us as soon as possible.

Your Profile

- Completed vocational training as an Aircraft Electronics Technician, Electronics Technician, Mechatronics Technician, a comparable technical qualification, or a degree in an engineering or technical field.
- Good computer skills, particularly with Windows operating systems and older computer hardware
- Good IT skills, basic network setup and understanding of network protocols.
- Familiarity with technologies such as RS-232, Ethernet, Fibre Optics and Microcontrollers.
- Ability to repair and replace hardware components, perform soldering and rework, troubleshoot and diagnose electrical and electronic faults, trace wiring and signal paths, measure and test electrical circuits using diagnostic equipment, interpret electrical schematics, and carry out component-level repairs
- Ability to work independently with a high level of personal responsibility.
- Knowledge of C++ programming language and experience in the aviation industry are an advantage.
- Fluent in spoken and written english
- Quick learner with strong teamwork skills, initiative, and enthusiasm.
- Strong interest in technical systems and aviation industry

Your Responsibilities

- Work as part of the simulator maintenance team.
- Independently perform maintenance and servicing of simulator hardware, including quality checks.
- Provide technical support during customer training operations.
- Analyze and diagnose faults, carry out repairs.
- Document maintenance activities, inspections, and quality checks.

What We Offer

- A friendly working environment in a small team with an open, collaborative culture and flat hierarchies.
- A responsible and varied role with exciting technical challenges.
- The opportunity to work on a unique Level D King Air B200 simulator—the only one of its kind in Europe.
- A positive workplace atmosphere and modern facilities.
- The chance to contribute to internal process improvements and help plan and implement the company's second simulator.

jobs.description:
Introduction

INM is an internationally leading centre for interdisciplinary research on (bio)hybrid materials, and their exploitation in materials-based solutions for a sustainable world with increasing digitalization and medical needs. Our research integrates materials chemistry, biological processes, physical analysis, and process engineering. We aim for leadership in the fields of opto-interactive, electro-integrative and bio-intelligent material systems. In these areas, we actively seize opportunities to transfer our scientific results into materials-driven innovation.

The INM research group, Bioprogrammable Materials, is looking for an enthusiastic Post-Doctoral Researcher with experience in microbial biotechnology and adaptive laboratory evolution (ALE). We combine synthetic biology, microbial engineering and sustainable materials research to develop innovative solutions for industrial and environmental challenges. We are seeking to fill a 2-year funded Post-Doctoral Researcher position as part of an Industrially-aligned European project developing sustainable biobased coatings. The role at INM focuses on identifying and ehancingmicrobes capable of degrading the polymeric coatings, thereby enabling future circularity and end-of-life strategies.

Identify microbes capable of degrading bio-based polymeric materials
Establish screening platforms to evaluate microbial degradation performance
Apply adaptive laboratory evolution (ALE) to improve degradation efficiency and substrate utilization
Characterize evolved strains using microbiological and molecular biology techniques
Collaborate closely with industrial and academic project partners
Contribute to project reporting, scientific publications and conference presentations
Actively participate in the research activities of the group
We are seeking a person with a doctoral degree in biotechnology, biochemistry, microbiology or related fields, with practical experience in adaptive lab evolution. The candidate will be part of an international, multi-disciplinary team in which English is the primary language of communication and reporting. Since we work on application-oriented research, candidates with entrepreneurial interests are appreciated.

A 2-year E13 TV-L 100% contract.
A dynamic, interdisciplinary, and international research environment with excellent, state-of-the-art infrastructure.
A cooperative, friendly and supportive environment, with plenty of opportunities to interact with other researchers, also outside the team and the institute.
The opportunity for training to support high-quality research and to further develop your profile.

Neuronal exocytosis is a highly regulated process that enables the rapid release of neurotransmitters from synaptic vesicles. Central to this process is the controlled assembly of SNARE protein complexes, which drive membrane fusion and are regulated by a network of associated proteins. The PhD project will investigate the structural and molecular mechanisms underlying SNARE complex assembly and function in membrane-like environments. A particular focus will be placed on the development and characterization of membrane-mimetic systems, including lipid nanodiscs and synthetic copolymers, to study SNARE complexes and their regulatory proteins under increasingly native-like conditions. Cryo-electron microscopy will be combined with complementary biochemical and biophysical approaches to characterize these systems at the molecular level.
The project offers the opportunity to work in an interdisciplinary structural biology environment at Forschungszentrum Jülich, with access to expertise in cryo-EM, NMR spectroscopy and X-ray crystallography. Cryo-EM studies will be conducted at the state-of-the-art facilities of the Ernst Ruska-Centre (ER-C) at Forschungszentrum Jülich. The expertise in NMR spectroscopy and macromolecular crystallography at IBI-7 offers further opportunities for complementary structural and biophysical characterization. This combination of methods will enable the candidate to address biological questions from different structural perspectives and to develop a broad expertise in modern structural biology. We are looking for a highly motivated candidate with:

A Master’s degree in biochemistry, molecular biology, structural biology, or a related field

Strong practical experience in protein biochemistry, including recombinant protein expression and purification
Previous hands-on experience with cryo-electron microscopy and/or cryo-EM sample preparation
Interest in membrane proteins, protein-protein interactions and structural biology
Ability to work independently as well as in an interdisciplinary research team
Good communication skills in English

jobs.occupation: IMPACT PORTFOLIO MANAGER (Fairer Futures Programmes) (Projektleiter/in / Projektmanager/in)
jobs.description:
Overview:

Fairtrade is the most recognized and trusted sustainability label, working to make trade fairer for people and planet.

For more than three decades, Fairtrade has been making an impact on the way trade works. We believe that every farmer and worker should have access to a better way of doing business, and a better way of living. 

Fairtrade International is an independent non-profit organisation representing more than two million small-scale farmers and workers worldwide. It owns the FAIRTRADE Mark, a registered trademark that appears on more than 37,000 products. Beyond certification, Fairtrade International and its member organisations (three producer networks and 19 national Fairtrade organisations) partner with producers and businesses, engage consumers, and advocate for a fair and sustainable future.

Unit’s description and purpose: 

The Global Impact unit strengthens the Fairtrade system by driving institutional learning and effectiveness through robust monitoring and evaluation systems. We are the hub for the analysis and communication of high-quality data and information about Fairtrade and its impact, as well as supporting strategy delivery. The unit includes the Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) team, which is the Fairtrade system’s hub for MEL which directly connects evidence to strategic decision for the Global Strategy, individual Fairtrade projects and global programmes, Standards, producer support, and more.

PRINCIPAL ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Role purpose: 

The Impact Portfolio Manager (Fairer Futures Programmes) is responsible for stewarding the MEL frameworks for several of Fairtrade’s global product programmes, the flagship programmatic vehicles through which Fairtrade delivers measurable impact for farmers and workers under its 2026–2028 Global Strategy. 

The manager will share responsibilities for a total of three programmes (cocoa, banana, coffee) with another manager, with product- and thematic-specific focus to be determined upon hire.

Working in close collaboration with Fairtrade Producer Networks, Global Product Teams, and the Digital Service Unit, the role ensures that both programmes are underpinned by robust, coherent, and actionable MEL, from framework design through data collection, reporting, evaluation, and learning. The position serves as one of Fairtrade International's primary MEL contact across programme discussions, representing the Global Impact unit in a system that spans FI, National Fairtrade Organizations, and Producer Networks. This role also contributes to the Global Impact unit's impact services offer, drawing on programme MEL expertise to identify and develop customized services for the Fairtrade system and external partners.

Main Responsibilities:            

- MEL Framework, Indicators, and Data Management. Steward and drive the development, maintenance, and continuous improvement of the Theory of Change and MEL framework for several of the Fairer Futures Programmes, working in close collaboration with Producer Networks and Global Product Teams. Steward the KPI and activity/output indicator set for both programmes, including maintaining metadata and monitoring data quality. Work with PN MEL staff, Global Product Teams, and where needed external consultants to ensure systematic consolidation of existing programme data and the design and implementation of regular data collection processes. Coordinate with the Information & Knowledge team on data cleaning, analysis, and visualisation.
- Stakeholder Engagement and Project MEL Alignment. OVERVIEW:

Fairtrade is the most recognized and trusted sustainability label, working to make trade fairer for people and planet.

For more than three decades, Fairtrade has been making an impact on the way trade works. We believe that every farmer and worker should have access to a better way of doing business, and a better way of living. 

Fairtrade International is an independent non-profit organisation representing more than two million small-scale farmers and workers worldwide. It owns the FAIRTRADE Mark, a registered trademark that appears on more than 37,000 products. Beyond certification, Fairtrade International and its member organisations (three producer networks and 19 national Fairtrade organisations) partner with producers and businesses, engage consumers, and advocate for a fair and sustainable future.

 Unit’s description and purpose: 

Global Products, Programs and Policy (GPPP) provides leadership to the Fairtrade system with selected product, program and policy intelligence. To this end GPPP provides information, tools and strategic direction as the main outputs. 

GPPP facilitates and contributes to coherent implementation of strategic plans within the Fairtrade system. GPPP develops new ways of delivering Fairtrade’s intended impact in a changing business environment and risk context.

PRINCIPAL ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

The Cocoa Manager is responsible for implementation of GPPP cocoa works based on work schedule agreed with the Senior Advisor Cocoa. The work will deliver measurable impact for farmers and workers under its 2026–2028 Global Strategy. 

The Cocoa Manager joins a team that works fluidly, sharing responsibilities across multiple workstreams supporting each other where the need is the greatest to achieve their objectives. The environment is dynamic and priorities can shift with external events impacting workplans.
